compliance_decision:
Compliance Answer: A Risk Management and Compliance Programme should include a risk-based approach to combating ML, TF, and PF with controls proportionate to the identified risks at business, client levels, as well as for new products. It must also have documented procedures on public compliance communication (PCC).
Relevant Regulatory Basis: FIC-Act-reference-guide.txt - Chunk 6143 and Guidance Not e7 & PCC sets out guidance on a risk-based approach, as well as the necessity for documentation in RMCPs regarding public compliance communication (PCC).
Explanation: The regulatory context specifies that accountable institutions are required to implement an RBA which includes proportionate controls based on identified risks and maintaining documented procedures. It also highlights PCC within a risk management framework, indicating its importance in the programme's structure for compliance communication with relevant authorities or bodies like FICC (Financial Intelligence Consolidation Centre).
